messages:
miriam: Heads-up: getting repeated OOMs on prod-serving-3 during a mid-sized burst. Suspect logits slab scheduling + kernel switch interplay. Attached quick profiler dump below.

samir: Can you paste the trace and the alloc timeline?

miriam: paste: ```
[2026-03-17T15:12:08Z] req=abcd kernel_choice=matmul_fast seq=512 batch=8 workspace_peak=1.8GiB logits_slab_used=512MiB activation_slab_used=1.2GiB kv_cache=700MiB OOM_at=workspace_alloc
Backtrace: runtime::alloc_workspace -> scheduler::pick_kernel -> slab_manager::claim_logit_slab
```

jordan: Hm looks like workspace allocation spikes right after matmul_fast selected for long seqs. That kernel increases temporary tensor footprint for logits packing. Could be the kernel selector not accounting for peak scratchpad.

kyle: Also seeing higher-than-expected KV cache bounce in the same window on canary logs. Batches with many short requests + one long request cause prefix KV thrash. When KV thrash is high, effective free memory drops -> slab handoffs fail.

miriam: Replayed locally with `--trace-allocs` and reproduced: `slab_reclaim_attempts=3, last_reclaim_failed=true, fallback_alloc=vmalloc -> OOM`.

jordan: Proposal: 1) make kernel selector estimate peak scratchpad per-kernel (not just steady-state) 2) prefer kernels with lower transient allocations for mixed-batch modes 3) add a soft cap on logits_slab per-tenant so activation slab can breathe.

samir: +1. Can we surgically reduce logits slab reservation from 768MiB -> 384MiB on prod-serving-3 as a canary? That should reduce risk and expose regressions.

kyle: Before making slab change, also suggest enabling per-batch KV eviction heuristic we sketched (LRU by token-age) — that could reduce instantaneous KV pressure. Small perf cost but worth it to avoid OOM.

miriam: I'll open canary: change `logits_slab_reserve` for prod-serving-3 to 384MiB and flip `kv_eviction_policy=token_age_lr`. Rolling 10% -> 50% -> 100% if stable.

perf-bot: [trace-summary] request-burst: 2026-03-17T15:11:30Z..15:13:00Z peak_qps=132 avg_latency_incr=+28% p99_latency=820ms OOM_count=7

jordan: After canary, collect `--alloc-map` and `--kernel-decisions` logs. We need to correlate kernel picks to scratchpad peaks. Also add a lightweight metric: `scratchpad_headroom` = free_mem - expected_peak_kernel_temp.

miriam: Will deploy now. If we still see OOMs at 50% roll, revert slab change and fallback to kernel-blocklist for problem model versions.

samir: One more idea: additive batching heuristic — if a batch contains a long-seq request, reduce batch size cap to avoid kernel choice that triggers high scratchpad. Worth trying as follow-up.

kyle: Agreed. Order of ops: 1) slab canary 2) kv_eviction 3) additive-batching throttling 4) kernel selector peak-estimation. Keep me posted.

miriam: Rolling 10% now (prod-serving-3-a). Will post results + `alloc-map` in this thread. :thumbsup:
